findings.title: fulfillment_stopped dispute decision has no effect: stopped items stay shippable and invisible to operations
findings.evidence: fulfillment_update checks ORDER_NOT_PAID, INVALID_ITEMS, BAD_TRANSITION, ITEM_REFUNDED and DEDICATION_NOT_DONE and never reads finance.disputes; dispute_record (stats_disputes.sql:522-531) only validates that the named items are 'preparing' and inserts the row; order_detail returns the 'disputes' key only when v_role = 'owner' (order_operations.sql:415); OrderView.tsx:689 makes a line choosable unless fullyRefunded; orders_alerts.toShip (486-492) and the to_ship filter (243-247) still count the stopped lines.
findings.impact: After a chargeback the owner records «إيقاف الشحن» (fulfillment_stopped) and believes shipping is stopped; the line still appears under «للشحن» for the operations member, who sees no dispute section at all and ships the goods. The bank has already taken the money back; the goods are gone too.
findings.proposed_fix: In fulfillment_update, when p_state = 'shipped', refuse with a new code (ITEM_DISPUTED, itemIds) any item named in item_ids of the latest row (max seq per kind, provider_ref) of a finance.disputes row with decision = 'fulfillment_stopped' whose target attempt belongs to this order; leave the same items out of order_lines_to_ship, the to_ship filter and orders_alerts.toShip; add a per-fulfilment 'stopped' boolean to order_detail for every role and grey the line in OrderView.
findings.prior_overlap: none; VERIFICATION.md 'P08 dispute proof' asks for an explicit fulfilment decision, and contract section 6 says the decision is only recorded

findings.title: notify_confirm_backlog can deadlock with a concurrent notify_subscribe through the shared rate_limits rows
findings.evidence: The hourly backlog loops over up to 200 pending rows in one transaction; for each it calls finance.notify_confirm_queue, which does `select ... for update` on the notification row (line 100) and then finance.rate_limit_take on the per-address row and on the shared 'notify-confirm:all' row (lines 111-114). rate_limit_take is `insert ... on conflict do update` (contacts_and_email.sql:62-70), so the updated finance.rate_limits row stays locked until commit. After the backlog has queued one mail it holds the 'all' row and then waits on the next notification row; a sign-up that already holds its own notification row (the upsert at line 212) and reaches rate_limit_take('notify-confirm:all') waits on the backlog. The file's lock-order comment (lines 30-34) names only the availability and notification rows.
findings.impact: Once an hour (minute 17), while at least two capped pending rows exist and a visitor signs up at that moment, PostgreSQL aborts one side with 40P01: the visitor's request answers 500 (notify.ts maps every non-54000 error to FAILED) or the backlog run fails and its mails wait another hour.
findings.proposed_fix: In finance.notify_confirm_backlog pick the rows with `for update skip locked` in the cursor query, so every candidate row is locked before any bucket is taken and the backlog never waits on a row a sign-up holds; or take the two buckets before the notification row lock in notify_confirm_queue.
findings.proof_recipe: Three psql sessions on a disposable stack. Prepare two pending rows N1, N2 (addresses a@x.test, b@x.test, confirm_sent_at null) whose 'notify-confirm:email' day bucket is spent, then clear a@x.test's bucket so N1 can be queued. S2: begin; select * from public.notifications where id = N2 for update; S1: select finance.notify_confirm_backlog(); (queues N1, locks the 'notify-confirm:all' rate_limits row, blocks on N2). S2: select finance.rate_limit_take('notify-confirm:all', repeat('0',64), 30, interval '1 day'); (blocks on S1). After deadlock_timeout one session reports ERROR 40P01 deadlock detected. Expected after the fix: S1 skips N2 and returns 1.
findings.prior_overlap: R8-04 (purge deadlock, fixed); the orchestrator recorded 'the backlog against a sign-up for the same row' as uncovered

findings.title: An erased buyer's address keeps receiving mail: kept orders keep customer_email and email_hash, so recovery, shipping, refund and file-ready mails still go to it
findings.evidence: privacy_buyer_erase redacts only the outbox rows that exist (lines 781-786) and deletes only erasable orders; a paid, under-review or refunded order keeps customer_email and email_hash (lines 799-812 report it as ACCOUNTING_RETENTION). Later producers address new mail from that snapshot: order_recover_apply (delivery.sql:235-252, `returning o.customer_email`, orders matched by email_hash), fulfillment_update (order_operations.sql:721-723), refund_succeed (stats_disputes.sql:212-215), paid_asset_set (delivery.sql:461-464). The erase writes no finance.email_suppressions row, and docs/privacy-data-map.md:86-88 does not say the address will still be mailed.
findings.impact: After Anas confirms an erasure, anyone who types that address into the order-recovery form makes the system mail an order link to it (3 per hour per address, 20 per day in all), and any later shipment, refund or file upload on a kept order mails it too. The person was told their data was erased; the operator has no step that stops it.
findings.proposed_fix: Have privacy_buyer_erase insert finance.email_suppressions (recipient_hash, 'manual') for the address (outbox_claim then closes any later row as 'suppressed') and say in the data map that a later legitimate purchase from the same address needs the suppression removed; or, if E08 decides transactional mail on kept orders must continue, state that in the data map and in the answer sent to the person.
findings.prior_overlap: I51 (1) covers the export's gaps only

findings.title: A confirmed subscriber whose address bounced stays confirmed: every restock queues a notice that is closed 'suppressed' and lands in the mail attention list, and a sign-up for such an address spends a daily confirmation slot
findings.evidence: availability_sweep's `due` CTE selects every status = 'confirmed' row below the revision and inserts one outbox row per subscriber (lines 374-384) without consulting finance.email_suppressions; outbox_claim then marks the row 'suppressed' (order_emails.sql:277-282) and outbox_attention lists status 'suppressed' rows that carry none of the excluded codes (order_emails.sql:421-423). notify_confirm_queue (lines 104-120) takes the address bucket and the day's 30 before the insert, also for a suppressed address. No migration moves a public.notifications row on a bounce or complaint.
findings.impact: After one hard bounce or complaint, each later restock of each variant that address confirmed adds a permanent «محظور» row to /admin/email's attention list that nobody can act on, and a stranger's sign-up of a bounced address burns one of the day's 30 confirmation mails on a row that can never be sent.
findings.proposed_fix: In the sweep's `due` CTE and in notify_confirm_queue skip rows whose finance.recipient_hash(n.email) is in finance.email_suppressions; or, in email_event_record, set that address's notifications to 'unsubscribed' when a suppression is inserted.

findings.title: The buyer privacy procedure does not send the operator to the contact-form steps for the same address
findings.evidence: Line 58: «a buyer request touches customers, orders and their records only, never `auth.users`»; the export and erase steps (lines 60-88) never mention public.contacts or privacy_erase_contacts; privacy_buyer_export (stats_disputes.sql:606-725) reads no contacts row and privacy_buyer_erase (751-827) deletes none. The contact-form section (lines 44-48) is a separate procedure with its own query and function.
findings.impact: A buyer who also wrote through the contact form with the same address gets an access or erasure answer that misses their messages unless the operator remembers the other section; the ledger line for the buyer then records a deletion that left personal data behind.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one line to the buyer section: also run the contact-form visitor steps for the same address (the export query and privacy_erase_contacts) and record both calls in the ledger.

findings.title: The availability notice says the item is available («توفّر») when the sweep fired on a preorder state (pre-order only, ships later)
findings.evidence: availability_sweep treats the public state 'preorder' as sellable (notifications.sql:365: `variant_public_state(...) in ('available', 'preorder')`; notify.test.ts:870 'counts a preorder as sellable'), and notify_email_data (order_emails.sql:137-156) carries no state, date or note, so renderAvailability always writes «توفّر … الذي طلبت أن نخبرك عنه» with the product page link.
findings.impact: A subscriber of an out-of-stock variant that the owner turns into a preorder (capacity and a future date) is mailed that the item is available; the page then offers «اطلب مسبقًا» with a delivery date. Dormant while preorder is off (Anas, Q05); live the day the owner switches a variant to preorder.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the public state and preorder_ships_on to notify_email_data and let renderAvailability say «أصبح متاحًا للطلب المسبق، يُشحن في <date>» for 'preorder'.

doc_claims_checked.claim: pg_cron runs one instance of a job at a time (a second instance queues) and schedules in GMT unless cron.timezone is set, so the every-minute availability_sweep never overlaps itself in production and the 03:37 and 03:47 purges run at 06:37 and 06:47 Riyadh
doc_claims_checked.where: https://github.com/citusdata/pg_cron (README: 'only one instance of each specific job at a time. If a second instance is triggered before the first finishes, it's queued'; 'Previously pg_cron could only use GMT time, but now you can adapt your time by setting cron.timezone')
doc_claims_checked.evidence: Fetched 2026-10-06. The SQL's 'two sweeps at once' defence (notifications.sql:30-34; notify.test.ts:810) is therefore only reachable by a manual call, which is harmless.
